Oral Judgment

This appeal is filed by the claimant challenging the judgment and award dated 16th February 2017,
passed by the XVI Additional Judge and M.A.C.T., Court of Small Causes, Bengaluru, (for short `the Tribunal'), in MVC No.3602/2016, seeking enhancement of compensation.

entities.text: XVI Additional Judge and M.A.C.T., Court of Small Causes, Bengaluru
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: NC: 2025:KHC:30613 HC-KAR 2.
For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to as per their ranking before the Tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case are that, on 13.05.2016, at about 1.30 p.m., the claimant was going on his Motor Cycle bearing No.KA-05-HE-2416 near Sathanuru Police Station at Sathanuru Town, at that time, another Motor Cycle bearing Registration No.KA-11-EC-9351 came from behind and dashed against the petitioner's motor cycle, due to the impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained severe injuries to his left leg.
Immediately he was shifted to Sathanuru Government Hospital for first aid and then shifted to Sanjay Gandhi Hospital, Bengaluru, for further treatment.

sentences.text: The injured claimant filed claim application claiming compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by him.
NC: 2025:KHC:30613 HC-KAR 5.
From the rival contentions of the parties, the Tribunal framed necessary issues, for its determination.

6. The claimant to prove his case examined three witnesses as PWs-1 to 3 and marked 11 documents,
as per Exs.P-1 to P-11.
Respondents did not examine any witness so also did not mark any documents.

7. The Tribunal considering the evidence on record granted compensation of a sum of Rs.3,46,000/-
with interest @ 9% from the date of petition till the date of payment, which is as follows :-
 Particulars Amount in Rs.
 Pain and sufferings 30,000/-
Medical expenses 25,000/-

Nourishment, conveyance and 25,000/-
 attendant charges  Loss of future income 1,64,000/-
 Loss of amenities 25,000/-

Future medical expenses 12,000/-
 Loss of income during laid up period 40,000/-
 NC: 2025:KHC:30613 HC-KAR

Permanent disability 25,000/-
 Total 3,46,000/-
Being aggrieved by the said award passed by the Tribunal, the claimant has filed the present appeal for enhancement of compensation.

sentences.text: Heard the arguments of the learned counsel appearing for the claimant as well as the respondent No.1/Insurer.

9. Learned counsel for the appellant/claimant submits that the claimant had sustained fracture,
implants were fixed, he was discharged on 27.05.2016 with an advise to follow up treatment for six months.
The Doctor Assessed the disability at 19% to the whole body, movement of leg was restricted and there is shortening of leg by one Inch.
It is further contended that the Tribunal has not granted sufficient amount under the head 'Pain and suffering and also under the head Nourishment, Conveyance and Attendant Charges.'

He was under rest for more than six NC:
2025:KHC:30613 HC-KAR months.
Therefore, loss of income during laid up period is to be enhanced.
The amount granted under the head 'loss of amenities and future medical expenses' is also on the lower side, and therefore, requested for enhancement of compensation to Rs.14,50,000/-.

10. Heard the arguments of learned counsel for both the parties.
11.
As per the evidence of PW.2 petitioner sustained fracture of shaft of left tibia in the accident.
He underwent surgery with implant i.e., CRIF with IMIL Nailing in Sanjay Gandhi Hospital, Bangalore.
He was an inpatient in the said hospital for 15 days from 13.05.2016 to 27.05.2026.

Petitioner also produced Ex.P.6 and as per the said records, he was advised to take follow up treatment and rest till September 2016, and thus he was under follow-up treatment for four to five months.
The Tribunal observed the total laid up period of the claimant/inured was five months,
Medical bills are produced under Ex.P7 and P8 for NC: 2025:KHC:30613 HC-KAR an amount of Rs.24,260/-.
Ex. P10
is the case sheet.
Petitioner paid Rs.17,000/- towards hospital charges and the remaining amount was paid through Chief Minister's Relief Fund and thus he spent and amount of Rs.7,216/- towards medical expenses.
The whole body disability was assessed at 19%.

The Tribunal has considered 30%
disability to the left lower limb and has considered 1/3rd of the same for assessment of the compensation.
12. Learned counsel for the appellant mainly contended that the disability be taken at 19% instead of 10%, which is opposed by the learned counsel for the Insurance Company.
13. Considering the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, this Court finds that the Tribunal has rightly considered 10% of the disability and it needs no interference.
The injured was aged 28 years, he was working as a Plumber.
As there is no evidence, regarding his income, the Tribunal has taken the notional income of NC: 2025:KHC:30613 HC-KAR the injured at Rs.8,000/- per month.

But as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, for the accidents that took place in the year 2016 the notional income is to be taken at Rs.9,500/- per month for the purpose of calculation.
Thus the loss of future income comes to Rs.9,500 x 12 x 17 x 10% = 1,93,800/-.
Conveyance and Attendant Charges needs to be enhanced to Rs.30,000/- instead of Rs.25,000/-.
Loss of income during laid up period comes to Rs.47,500/- (Rs.9,500 x 5).
This Court finds no reason to interfere with the amounts awarded under other heads.

was granted towards permanent disability and it is to be deleted.
Therefore, the said amount of Rs.25,000/- be deleted.

15. Accordingly, following amount of compensation is awarded:

Medical expenses 25,000/-
 Special diet, conveyance and attendant 30,000/-

 (Rs.9,500/- x 5)

Loss of amenities and unhappiness 25,000/- Future medical expenses 12,000/-
 Total 3,63,300/-
 Amount awarded by the Tribunal 3,46,000/-
 Enhancement 17,300/-
16.

In the result, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER i) The Appeal is allowed in part.
 ii) The judgment and award dated  16.02.2017, passed in MVC.No.3602/2016, by the XVI Additional Judge and M.A.C.T., Court of Small Causes, Bengaluru, stands modified.
